paper.title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
paper.summary: The appearance of a scene is determined by the albedo, roughness, metallicity and normal of every point on its surface, and by the light that reaches it, its irradiance. Recovering these intrinsics from images is ambiguous, and methods that predict them per pixel give the same surface point a different decomposition in every view. We introduce PointX, a simple feed-forward model that predicts intrinsics per 3D surface point instead. A multi-view transformer encodes a set of unposed images, and for any queried surface point, PointX pools the point's tokens across the views in which it appears and decodes the point's intrinsics once. paper.title: Antiferromagnetic phase of MnTe2: spin-order-induced renormalization of phonon Raman spectrum
paper.summary: Recently, two modes of spin wave excitations (magnons) were detected in Raman scattering spectra of MnTe2. It is an unconventional magnet that features a pyrite-type crystal structure hosting a non-collinear, non-coplanar antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin order below the Néel temperature. In this brief communication, the focus is primarily on the effect of spin ordering on lattice dynamics (phonons) that has been established through temperature (5 - 300 K), linear polarization angle (0 deg - 360 deg) and external magnetic field (up to 16 T) dependent measurements. paper.title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
paper.summary: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). paper.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
paper.summary: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. paper.title: BioLoom: Scaling Biomedical Vision-Language Models by Learning from the Structure of Scientific Articles
paper.summary: The development of biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) with contrastive image-text pretraining has been driven by scaling to increasingly large and diverse image-text datasets. Beyond scaling, further progress can come from learning richer representations from existing data. We hypothesize that the structure of scientific literature itself provides an additional source of supervision: figures, panels, captions, and accompanying article text encode rich relationships across modalities. Yet, treating these as independent image-text pairs overlooks their relationships. To address this limitation, we incorporate these structural relationships into contrastive image-text supervision.
